To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SREBPs are a family of membrane bound transcription factors that are involved in the control of endogenous lipid synthesis.

1) SREBPs are master regulators of lipid synthesis and metabolism; 2) the SREBP iso-forms are differentially expressed in different tissues; 3) the regulation of each SREBPs isoform is unique; and 4) the activation of SREBPs is mainly controlled by intracellular cholesterol and insulin.
the three isoforms of SREBPs have different functions in the regulation of lipid homeostatic pathways.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of SREBP iso forms in lipid metabolism and the regulation of SREBP expression and activity.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate SREBP 3 isoforms and their role in lipid homeostasis.
the regulation of SREBP transcription factor activity and the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms that regulate the expression of SREBPs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SREBP transcription factor is the major regulator of cellular lipid synthesis.
SREBP proteins are the master regulators of lipid metabolism and that the regulation of SREBPs is a major target for the treatment of dyslipidemias and obesity.
SREBPs are key regulators of cellular lipid homeostasis and that they are the major transcription factors involved in the control of lipid homeostatic balance in the cell.
